title: Reset Button Style Property
content: ### Objective Reset button item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset → The button item properties are now being reset back to default value.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for resetting button item properties to their default values in version 2.5.0 through the Object Browser's Button Tab.

title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide All Tape Measure
content: ### Objective Show or hide all of the tape measures in the window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Avatar ▶ Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window ▶ Avatar Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Avatar Measurements → All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to toggle the visibility of all tape measures associated with the avatar in the 3D window.

title: Convert to Curve Point (AI Bezier Curve)
content: ### Objective Convert AI Bezier Curve's Segment Points to Free Curve Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point ### Operation #### AI Bezier Curve 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2. Right click on the AI Bezier Curve or the Segment point on the curve. → The right click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Convert to Curve Point. → The selected AI Bezier curve is converted to a Free Curve as its AI Bezier curve handles disappear and necessary Free Curve Points are added to maintain its original curvature. #### AI Bezier Curve Handles 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern / Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Curve Point 2. Click on the AI Bezier curve to be converted. → Its AI Bezier curve handles appear. 3. Right click on the end point of the handle and select Convert to Curve Point on the pop-up menu. → Its original curvature is maintained as Free Curve Points are added.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for converting AI Bezier curve segment points into Free Curve points while preserving the original curvature.

title: Apply Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Apply buttonhole styles or fabric material (.zfab) onto buttonholes as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ### Operation #### Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor 1. Click on a buttonhole and select a buttonhole style in the Property Editor. → The selected buttonhole style is now being applied to the buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to Selected Patterns → The buttonhole style is now being applied to the selected buttonhole. #### Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style 1. Select a buttonhole. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Assigned to New Fabric → A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to apply and manage buttonhole styles and fabric materials within the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: Create 2D Button Measurement
content: ### Objective View button position from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. Select a button with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center 3. Select the desired 2D measurement options of the left/right/up/down. → The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to view and adjust the 2D measurements of button positions in the Pattern outline using the Button Property Editor.

title: Button List Window
content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on the Default Button feature, explaining its persistent modification capabilities and limitations within the button list settings.

title: Express Air Pressure
content: ### Objective Use the Pressure value to create an effect of air or padded materials such as padded jumpers, pillows, cushions, balloons, etc. ### Location Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Pressure ### Operation 1. Select a Pattern to express pressure with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Pressure 3. Adjust the value as desired.
content_description: Discover how to effectively simulate the effects of air and padding in materials like cushions and balloons by adjusting the pressure settings in our pattern editor.

title: Line Tack on Avatar
content: ### Objective Create lines on Garment and avatar and tack to each other by lines. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 3D window tool bar Line tack on Avatar tool ### Operation 1. Select the tool according to the Location above. 2. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. 3. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Once a line is created on the garment, 3D garment will be transparent, can create line on the avatar directly. 4. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. 5. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. * During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. * Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. * When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create and connect lines on garments and avatars using the 3D window tool, enhancing your design process.

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Tape Measurement
content: ### Objective Take avatar's measurements such as arm length, back length from projected points. Basic Tape Measurement measures following by its surface curves. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Tape Measurement 2. Click on a point to begin the length measurement. → Temporary line appears in purple. 3. Click on any points that need to be included in the process, and double click to end the measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for accurately measuring an avatar's dimensions, such as arm and back length, using the Basic/Surface Tape Measurement tool in the 3D interface.

title: 3D File (USD) Import/Export
content: ### USD Import/Export ### Objective Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in USD file and they are compatible with other 3D software. ### Location #### USD Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD #### USD Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD ### Operation #### USD Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → Import USD window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### USD Import Detail Settings Scale | Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. ---|--- Move Garment to Start Position | Jump to the position of the start frame of the motion where the garment was loaded and move it. Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame. Transition Animation | A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motion’s first pose in stages, and is created when the avatar’s current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. #### USD Export 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD → Save File window appears. 2. Select desired location to store, and click Save. → Export USD window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### USD Export Detail Settings Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. ---|--- #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. | Image Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel ---|--- Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Animation | Entire Region: Save the recorded garment's animation entirely. Play Region Only: Only the garment animation in the play area is saved.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive guidelines for importing and exporting garments in USD format using Marvelous Designer, ensuring compatibility with various 3D software.

title: Show/Hide Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Show or hide all buttons and buttonholes. ### Location 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) ▶ Show Button → All buttons and buttonholes are now being hidden. 2. Follow the indicated guideline once again. → All hidden buttons and buttonholes are now being displayed.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to easily toggle the visibility of all buttons and buttonholes in the 3D garment display.

title: OBJ TRIM: Glue OBJ Trim
content: ### Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver3.0.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ ### Operation #### Glue OBJ Trim 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Select desired OBJ file and click OK to load. 3. In the pop-up menu, select Load as Trim for the Object Type, and click OK. 4. Click the loaded OBJ with the Select/Move tool. → Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. 5. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. → OBJ preview tags along the mouse. 6. Click on the desired location. → Selected OBJ automatically attaches to the place. 7. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. ※ Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. 8. Activate Simulation. → OBJ is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. ※Note: You can select multiple OBJ trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) Delete OBJ Trim 1. Right click on the OBJ trim. → OBJ is now being selected and a pop-up menu appears. ※ Note: Relevant menu above does not appear for OBJ trims that are not glued to the Garments. 2. Click on Delete to remove it. → Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for importing, gluing, and simulating 3D OBJ trims onto garments using Objective Glue version 3.0.0.

title: Align
content: ### Objective Align Patterns and Internal Shapes based on various standards (ver2.5.0). ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ Left/ Center/ Right/ Top/ Middle/ Bottom ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/ Internal Shape) ▶ Align ▶ Left/ Center/ Right/ Top/ Middle/ Bottom →The Patterns or/and Internal Shapes align to the Pattern or Internal Shape that is right clicked on. ※Note: You can also align Pattern outlines or Internal Lines using the 2.png Edit Pattern tool. However, be mindful that the aligning segments may transform their Patterns or Internal Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for aligning patterns and internal shapes using the Transform Pattern tool and right-click pop-up menu options in accordance with various standards.

title: Edit Sewing Line Length
content: ### Objective Adjust Sewing Line length. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Click and drag either end point of the Sewing Line to adjust its length. ※ Note: While clicking and dragging the end of the Sewing Line in the 2D Window, right-click and type in the Distance Moved or Total Length in the Moving Distance window.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting the length of the Sewing Line in the 2D/3D editing interface of the sewing module.

title: Mirror Paste Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 2. Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. 3. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. → Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. 4. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. ※ Note: * Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. * When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.
content_description: This webpage serves as a step-by-step guide for using the Mirror Paste function to efficiently copy and mirror buttonholes in your design.

title: Add Arrangement Point
content: ### Objective Add new Arrangement Point on the Bound Volume as needed. ※ Note: Without corresponding Bounding Volume, the Arrangement Point is invisible. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Add Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Add → A new arrangement point called "Arrangement Point" is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2\. Set details for Arrangement Point. Name | Changes the name of the Arrangement Point. ---|--- Arrangement | Arrangement BV | Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point to be placed. X | Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y | Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset | Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction | The direction in which the Pattern wrapped around the Avatar. ※ Note: #### Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set Symmetric Arrangement Point. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default (ver3.0). _R _L Follow the indicated steps below to save the Avatar and Arrangement Points, and reload to apply the setting. Light-blue outer line appears around the Symmetric Arrangement Point. #### Save Avatar: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Avatar #### Save Arrangement Point: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Arrangement Point ▶ Save
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adding and configuring new Arrangement Points on the Bound Volume within the Avatar Editor, ensuring users can effectively customize their avatars' positioning and symmetry settings.

title: Convert: Curve Points & Segment Points
content: ### ### Objective Convert multiple Segment Points on single or multiple Patterns to Curve Points. Convert multiple Curve Points on a single or multiple Patterns to Segment Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select all Segment Points / Curve Points to be converted to the other point type. 3. Right click to access the pop-up menu. Then select Convert to Curve Point / Convert to Segment Point. Select the option Maintain Curve or Convert Only. (ver. 2024.2) → All selected Point type - Segment points / Curve Points are converted to the other type. ### Convert Options (ver. 2024.2) Maintain Curve | Adds curve points automatically to the line to maintain the line curvature / straight line result. ---|--- Convert Only | Convert without adding curve points on the line. The curved line / straight line result will be affected slightly.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for converting Segment Points to Curve Points and vice versa within 2D patterns, offering options to maintain curvature or convert directly.

title: Cut/ Cut & Sew
content: ### Objective Cut a single 2D Pattern into two or more pieces using Internal Lines (ver2.3.0). ### Location #### Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern #### Trace Tool (ver2.4.0) Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace ### Operation #### Transform Pattern/ Edit Pattern Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut & Sew. → The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut & Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. #### Trace Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Trace 2D Toolbar ▶ Trace 2. Right click on the Internal Line/Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Cut or Cut & Sew. → The Pattern is divided based on the selected Internal Line/Shape. If you select Cut & Sew, Sewing Lines are established between the divided Patterns. ※ Note: With the Trace tool, you can Cut or Cut & Sew Patterns using the Baselines as well.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for cutting and transforming 2D patterns into multiple pieces using the Transform Pattern/Edit Pattern and Trace tools.

title: License Key Update With Dongle
content: ### License Key Update ### Objective Set the dongle key when the Network License users want to update their dongle key info. (Currently only available on Windows PC) ### Operation A C2V file is a file sent from the users to the Marvelous Designer Support Team and a V2C file is the other way around (sent from MD back to user). This method enables the users to update their account info / product type / the number of licenses without changing the HASP dongle key. Preparations →HASP dongle key →Update_License.exe file →C2V file →V2C file ### 1\. Creating a C2V file 1\. Plug the HASP Key (dongle) into your computer. 2\. Download and execute the the RUS executable file located at the bottom of this post. 3\. Create C2V file by clicking on Collect Information as below. ![1_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438777969561) 4\. Once the C2V file successfully created, a message will be printed as below. ![1__.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438788454297) 5\. Submit your C2V file through [**this page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com ### 2\. Updating a License Key using V2C file 1\. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select Update/Attach in Options on the left. [ACC Page Link](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778524825) 3\. Click Choose File to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438794667161) 4\. Click Apply File. ![4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778839449) 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778982297) ### 3\. Double checking on updated License Key If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Make sure all the information is in this part. 3\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438789202841) 4\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly. ![7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438774056729)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for Network License users to update their dongle key information using C2V and V2C files on Windows PCs.

title: Fold/Sew Pleats
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing ### Operation #### Pleats Fold 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Fold 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Fold 2. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. → Pleats Fold window appears. 3. Select a desired type of pleats. → Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. ※ Note: Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) 4. Check Reverse Direction option as needed. → The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. 5. Click OK button to complete. #### Pleats Sewing 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Sewing 2. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. 3. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. → Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). 4. Click on the end point to complete. → The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and sewing various pleat styles using the 2D Pattern tool, enabling users to enhance their sewing projects with precision and creativity.

Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-Click on an Internal Line or Point. → The pop-up menu appears. 3. title: Copy/Paste Tack
content: ### Objective Copy and paste tack. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack ### Operation #### Copy/Paste Tack 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Copy → The selected tack is copied. 4. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. 5. Select Paste or Mirror Paste. → Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. → Any tack outside of the Pattern does not appear in the 3D window. 6. Click the desired location to paste the tack. #### Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. → Selected tack is duplicated to the exact same location on its Symmetric Pattern. ※Note: Selected tacks need to be within the same Pattern in order to be duplicated to their Symmetric Patterns.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying, pasting, and duplicating tacks within sewing patterns using the Edit Tack function in the 3D Toolbar.

title: [Size Editor] Adjust Avatar Size (ver. 10)
content: ### ### ### Objective Create an avatar with your own measurements. As Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Avatar Size ### Operation 1. Load an Avatar (.avt). Only the avatars provided in ver. 10 V2 and above can be adjusted. 2. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Avatar Size → Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. 3. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Select Avatar** | Select the Avatar to be edited. This option only appears when two or more Avatars are in the 3D window. **Total Body** | Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. **Height** | Assign Avatar's height. ※Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Degree of Accuracy based on Height Measure Standard: HPS Height > Inseam > Total Height **Total Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. ※Note: It is more accurate to assign height with either HPS Height or Inseam option as individual has different head length. The Total Height option is not recommended as it has the lowest accuracy. **HPS Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. **Inseam** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. **Width** | Select and insert desired value as the standard of the overall body width **Details** | Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. Due to a technical reason, a small error may be generated even after inserting a specific measure. The error appears in parentheses next to each measurement and the real measurement can be checked with the measure appears on the Avatar. Edit the Avatar based on the measure appears on the Avatar as the numbers appear in the Avatar Editor only shows the measurements assigned by users. ※Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Each measurement can be checked with the measure that appears on the Avatar. **Basic** | Use the Basic option when only a small amount of body measurements are available. Unassigned body parts are automatically adjusted based on the real body scan data and the measurements inserted by the user. **Advanced** | Use the Advanced option when available body measurements are abundant. When all measurements under the Advanced options are not available, please use the Basic option to create more realistic body as unassigned measurements are fixed with the default values pre-assigned to each option. **Show All Measurements/** **Show Editable Measurements** | By default, only editable measurements appear in the window. To view all measurements, click the Show All Measurements icon. * Use the Save button to save the adjusted measurements and use the Open button to reload. However, any measurements created with lower versions are not compatible.
content_description: Create a personalized avatar using precise measurements, enhanced by real body scan data for a realistic and customizable 3D representation of yourself.

title: Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting
content: 1\. By updating the graphics card driver, you can solve and prevent graphics card-related problems that may occur while using the Marvelous Designer software. 2\. Guides you on how to properly connect your desktop graphics card and monitor. ### Applicable for: All users of Marvelous Designer software * * * # **Common Problems** 1\. OpenGL version warning appears when running Marvelous Designer software as shown in the figure below. ![Screen_Shot_2022-10-20_at_9.37.19_PM.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438272879385) 2\. Graphics/texture errors or rendering images appear strange while running Marvelous Designer software. 3\. If the Marvelous Designer GPU-simulation or GPU-rendering speed is lower than the expected performance of your computer's specifications. * * * ## How to Update Graphics Card Driver Step 1) Find out the product name of the graphics card (GPU) installed in your desktop computer or laptop. * As shown in the figure below, you can find the model name of your graphics card (GPU) in the Performance tab of Windows Device Manager. ![002_Task_Manager.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438289814041) Step 2) Search and download the latest driver matching the product name from each manufacturer's website. * Note that even if the graphics card model name looks the same or similar, the drivers for laptops and desktops, and for workstations and servers are different. Search for and install the driver for the type of computer you are using. * [AMD Radeon Driver Download (Link)](https://www.amd.com/en/support) * [Nvidia Driver Download (Link)](https://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx?lang=en) * [Intel Graphics Driver Download (Link)](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download-center/home.html) Step 3) Run the downloaded driver file. It is recommended to install with administrator privileges. * A computer reboot may be required after driver installation. Follow the on-screen instructions. ![003_RunAsAdministrator.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438273265561) * * * ## Connecting the monitor and graphics card correctly As shown in the figure below, if the monitor cable is connected to the CPU built-in GPU, the built-in GPU is mainly used instead of the external graphics card. OpenGL version warnings may occur when running Marvelous Designer in this situation. ![004_Connectors.JPG](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438293924505) **How to fix** Step 1) Save the files you are working on and turn off the computer completely. Step 2) Connect the monitor cable to the external graphics card and turn on the computer. Connect all monitor cables to the external graphics card, even when using more than one monitor. Step 3) If there is no screen output on the monitor, try reconnecting the monitor power. **See also** * Supported monitor cable types vary depending on the graphic card and monitor. * If you are using the latest monitor and the latest graphic card, most support HDMI or DP (DisplayPort). * Find the right cable for your monitor and graphics card. [Saved search (Link)](https://www.google.com/search?q=monitor+cable+types&oq=monitor+cable) * * * ## Read more * Marvelous Designer software automatically detects the graphics card and driver installed in the computer when launching, and displays a warning if an unsupported graphics card or outdated driver is found. Please refer to the guide above to solve the problem. * If you are using a laptop with an Nvidia graphics card, the laptop will have either an AMD processor or an Intel processor with integrated graphics GPU and Nvidia GPU, respectively, depending on the situation. If an openGL-related error appears while using the Marvelous Designer software, select 'High-performance Nvidia processor' in the Nvidia control panel as shown below and click Apply. ![005_Nvidia_Control_Panel.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438278923929) * If you set Windows Update to 'Auto', it will automatically install the latest graphics card driver. However, the driver provided by the graphics card manufacturer's website is more up-to-date than the Windows update version. * It is recommended to update the graphics card driver at least once every 6 months. It helps with Marvelous Designer software as well as all other graphics programs and overall system performance and stability. * To check GPU usage in Windows, select GPU in the Performance tab of Task Manager as shown below. For Windows 11 users, use a dedicated utility like [GPU-z (freeware, download link)](https://www.techpowerup.com/gpuz/) ![006_CUDA.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438294373401) * If you are using a Mac, the graphics card driver is included in macOS. If you update to the latest macOS, the latest graphics card driver is also installed. * To check CPU-GPU usage on Mac, use the Activity Monitor app built-in to macOS. * Also check the [Marvelous Designer system requirements ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219834649)for graphics card-related information.
content_description: This webpage offers essential guidance for Marvelous Designer users on updating graphics card drivers and properly connecting monitors to resolve common graphics-related issues.

title: Group Internal Lines and Shapes
content: #### **New in 2025.1** Group with Transform Pattern Group with Edit Pattern Select or Edit Grouped Items with Transform Pattern Ungroup with Transform Pattern #### Group the selected internal lines and pattern shapes. #### ### **Group with Transform Pattern** 1. Select 2 or more internal lines or shapes. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Group** to group the selected items. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48977895497881)** • A shortcut key for grouping is available. **Function** | **Shortcut** ---|--- **Group** | Windows: Ctrl + G / Mac: Command + G **Ungroup** | Windows: Ctrl + Delete / Mac: Command + Delete; or Command + Fn + Backspace • When grouping or ungrouping internal lines or shapes on one side of a symmetric or half-symmetric pattern, both sides are impacted. • Group relationship is maintained for pattern copy & paste, symmetrical copy, cutting, and merging cases. #### ### ### **Group with Edit Pattern** 1. Select the whole group of internal lines and segment points. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Group** to group the selected items. **📝Note:** When selecting an incompleted line or point of Internal Line or Shape, the Group menu will not show. #### ### ### **Select or Edit Grouped Items** **with Transform Pattern** 1. Click on the grouped internal lines or shapes to select the whole group. 2. Click again on the individual internal lines or shapes to select individual lines or shapes. #### ### ### **Ungroup with Transform Pattern** 1. Select the grouped internal lines or shapes. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Ungroup** to remove the group relationship of the selected items.
content_description: Discover the new grouping and ungrouping features in 2025.1 that enhance your design workflow by allowing you to easily manage internal lines and pattern shapes.
